qt: to the Commission Majdouline Sbai (Verts/ALE) Subject:
India’s pressure on EU legislation on EU aluminium scrap export restrictions

In September 2025, regarding the EU-US trade deal, the European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security, Interinstitutional Relations and Transparency Maroš Šefčovič declared that ‘our regulatory autonomy, is not for sale. Ever’1. In November 2025, the Commissioner announced that ‘we are launching the preparatory work on a new measure to address the issue of aluminium scrap leakage’2. He added that ‘scrap is a strategic commodity given its important contribution to circularity and decarbonisation, […] as well as to our strategic autonomy’3. Initially announced as a trade measure, it seems to have been withdrawn because of pressure from India, which is a big buyer of EU aluminium scrap, during trade negotiations4. The Commission now envisages a delegated act under the Waste Shipment Regulation56. But again, there are pressures from India. Can the Commission confirm: 1.
Whether the negotiations on a free trade agreement with India played a role in the removal of the announced trade measure?
That the envisaged delegated act will not exclude India from the measure on aluminium scrap exports?
Whether the initial envisaged measure could still be put forward, including India in its scope?
